meta.title: The Badass Hangar
meta.subtitle: Pop-culture blueprints translated into real Corvette Workshop parts.
meta.disclaimer: These are fan-made part recommendations, not official Hello Games content. Silhouettes are approximated with the modules that exist in the Voyagers update -- part costs are calculated from data/parts.json, so the totals update automatically if you edit the database.
meta.costNote: Totals are the Unit cost of buying every non-optional module at the Workshop vendor. Salvage-only parts are priced at their estimated market value.
meta.naniteNote: Add roughly 85,000 Nanites to take the finished Corvette from C-class to S-class at the Starship Outfitting terminal (first upgrade: 10,000 Nanites).

blueprints.name: Millennium Falcon
blueprints.blurb: A flattened saucer with an offset bridge and a pair of wide rear thruster banks. The whole trick is keeping the hull low and wide while hiding the landing bay inside.
blueprints.signatureLine: She may not look like much, but she's got it where it counts.

parts.note: Offset bridge pod on the port rim - the single most important piece for the Falcon read.
Three flat Hab sections form the main saucer mass.
Low corridors to widen the disc without adding height.
Internal hangar keeps the underside perfectly smooth.
Twin Pyrodrive main engines = the two big rear nozzles.
Widebody thruster pods flank the mains for the flattened thruster bank.
Shield reactor: she survives what she cannot outrun.
Quad-laser look - mount both on the dorsal saucer.
Concussion missile feel: hidden behind the boarding ramp.
Hover pads instead of legs keeps the disc silhouette flat.
Armour cowlings bowed around the saucer rim.
Fairings clad the engine block.
Optional vent plates to smooth the hull joins.

buildTips: Build the hull 1 floor, 2 at most. The Falcon must read as a pancake from above.
Place the two Pyrodrive mains first at the stern, then work the saucer forward from them.
Mount the Ambassador cockpit off-centre on the starboard rim, never on the centreline.
Hide the landing bay inside the disc - any visible door geometry breaks the illusion.

blueprints.name: T-65 X-Wing
blueprints.blurb: Four S-Foils in a cross, four slim thruster pods, four wing-tip cannons. Small, cheap, absurdly fast to fly in third person.

parts.note: Arrowhead nose reads as the X-Wing's pointed fuselage.
The whole ship. Two upper, two lower, splayed at 30 degrees.
One slim sublight thruster at the root of each foil.
Central Arcadia booster as the main powerplant - salvage-only, but it is the only way to keep the four thruster pods propelling a hull this small.
Wing-tip cannons. Tip-mount them, never centre-mount.
Exotic powershield to survive a TIE swarm.
Pulse engine reactor for boost-heavy flying.
Doubles as the astromech socket and your only inventory space.
Flush bay keeps the fuselage line clean.
Slim skids, one under each lower foil.
Winglet detail on the upper foils.

buildTips: Symmetry is mandatory here - the cross pattern is the entire silhouette.
Keep the part count under 25. An X-Wing that is 15 parts too big stops looking like an X-Wing.
Splay the foils outward rather than flat; it reads far better in third-person flight.
This is the cheapest blueprint in the hangar - a great first real build.

blueprints.name: Imperial Star Destroyer
blueprints.blurb: A 3-floor wedge the size of a small freighter. You are building the whole dagger shape out of Habs and Walkways, then bolting turrets down both edges.

parts.note: The bridge tower - stack it on the highest dorsal Hab.
The wedge body. Widen as you go aft.
Dorsal spine and the tapered nose point.
Engine block transitions.
Second bay hidden in the ventral trench.
Long-range capitol reactor banks.
Triple bell nozzles across the stern - the classic rear wall of light.
Broadside turrets along the dorsal edges.
Ventral trench guns.
Edge plating to sharpen the wedge.
Wing modules flattened into hull edges.
Nothing lighter will hold this up.

buildTips: Build the wedge from the stern forward: widest hab cluster aft, tapering walkways to a point at the nose.
Three floors maximum. The bridge tower makes it look like four, but keep the tower after the top deck.
Heavy Landing Gear is effectively mandatory at this mass.
Symmetry matters more than detail - the wedge shape does all the work.

blueprints.name: UNSC Pelican
blueprints.blurb: Blunt nose, boxy tail, chin ramp and a big dorsal engine block. The ugly-but-perfect utilitarian read - and it flies superbly because you barely added any wings.

parts.note: Blunt industrial flight deck, twin-seat look.
The troop compartment - armoured plating look.
Ribbed tail section.
The chin ramp. Mount it as low and forward as you can.
Twin dorsal booster block.
Vectoring jets below the engine block.
Wing-mounted launcher pods.
Chin gun.
Stubby boxy wings with the lift pods.
Fairings around the engine block.
Heavy struts, nose gear forward of the ramp.
Third contact point under the tail.

buildTips: Keep it 2 floors with a chunky, boxy rear third - the Pelican is not sleek.
The chin ramp wants to sit slightly proud of the nose, not flush.
Mount both torpedo pods on the same wing line for the classic silhouette.
Great ship to actually fly: the short wings keep the hitbox tight.

blueprints.name: The Rocinante
blueprints.blurb: A hard-edged brick with a spinal rail of weapons and one absurdly powerful engine. The most 'it just works' build in the hangar - basically a proper Corvette with a rocket bolted on the back.
blueprints.signatureLine: The Rocinante is a legitimate salvage.

parts.note: Nose bridge, slightly offset up for the Roci's raised cockpit.
The Roci's belly hangar - invisible from outside.
Single Epstein-style main drive. The most important part on the ship.
Vectoring attitude jets.
Rapid-fire PDC batteries, one per flank.
Dorsal torpedo tubes.
Radiator plates - the Roci spins them out under load.
Shoulder plating.
Tall legs - leaves room for a refiner underneath.

buildTips: Two floors, long and narrow. Resist the urge to widen it.
Keep the weapon bays symmetrical down the flanks - they are the ship's identity.
One main engine, one nozzle. Do not twin it.
This is the best all-round 'actually usable in combat' blueprint in the hangar.

blueprints.name: USS Enterprise
blueprints.blurb: Saucer, neck, secondary hull, two nacelles on pylons. The hardest silhouette in the hangar because NMS has no saucer module - you cheat with cowlings and diffusers, and it works better than it has any right to.

parts.note: Set into the top of the saucer as the bridge dome.
Bowed around the nose in a circle to fake the primary saucer.
Fill the saucer gaps and clad the secondary hull.
Saucer mass plus the engineering hull.
Two for the neck, one for the pylon spar.
Warp reactor. Zenith is the correct choice here, thematically and mechanically.
Mounted on the pylons as nacelles.
Nacelle end caps.
Phaser banks on the saucer rim.
Deflector dish. Yes, really called that.
Nacelle pylons.
Third contact point hidden under the secondary hull.

buildTips: Nacelles go up and back at roughly 30 degrees - flat nacelles read as a cargo ship instead.
Keep the saucer 1 floor. Any thicker and the neck cannot support the look.
Zenith reactors give you the absurd warp range an explorer deserves.
This build eats parts fast. Trim optional plating first if you approach the 160 cap.

blueprints.name: Serenity
blueprints.blurb: Neck forward, fat tail, spinny engine thing at the back. A perfect 'flying base' Corvette: hab-heavy, walkway-rich, and legitimately pleasant to live in.
blueprints.signatureLine: I am a leaf on the wind.

parts.note: Small bridge on top of an extended neck.
The neck. Long, thin, forward of the body.
The fat mid-body hold.
The rear cargo ramp.
The big rear engine that spins in atmosphere.
Side thruster pods.
Dorsal defence guns.
The two rear fins.
Heat shielding on the tail.
Three tall legs - Serenity lands on legs, always.

buildTips: The neck is the whole silhouette: 3 walkways forward of the hab stack, nothing else.
Three legs, evenly spaced. It should look like it squats when parked.
Prioritise Habs over weapons - this is a live-aboard ship, so max your inventory slots.
Add the refiner and an indoor bed once built; this is the best 'flying base' blueprint.

blueprints.name: Viper Mk II
blueprints.classification: Mk II Viper space superiority fighter
blueprints.blurb: Three engines, three kinetic cannons, two stubby wings. The smallest viable Corvette in the hangar and the fastest thing you can legally build.

parts.note: Twin main drives with the flame nozzles.
Wing-root thrusters either side of the centre nozzle - the Viper's unmistakable triple cluster.
Wing-tip + nose kinetic guns. Deadeye is the only cannon that reads as a slug-thrower.
Manoeuvrability reactor. Nothing else makes sense on a Viper.
Short swept foils.
Minimum legal habitation - keeps the mass down.

buildTips: Under 30 parts total. If it starts looking bulky, you have overbuilt.
Keep the three engines tight and central - the missile cluster read comes from proximity.
Weapons on the tips of both foils plus the nose.
This is the fastest and most agile blueprint here; a Ceto reactor would ruin it.

blueprints.name: SSV Normandy SR-2
blueprints.blurb: Sleek swept hull, deep-set bridge, twin engine pods and a dorsal wing pair. A very natural fit for NMS parts - the parts pool basically wants to build this ship.
blueprints.signatureLine: The Normandy is the tip of the spear.

parts.note: Deep-set bridge, set back from the nose tip.
The Kodiak hangar. Keep it fully enclosed.
Twin Arcadia boosters = the SR-2's engine pods. Salvage-only, but worth the hunt.
Tantalus drive core: enormous range, quiet running.
Thanix-style spinal cannon read.
Javelin torpedo bays.
The swept dorsal wings.

buildTips: Long and low: 2 floors, narrow waist, tapered nose.
Set the cockpit one part back from the very tip - then plate over the tip for the SR-2's blunt prow.
Mount the two Arcadia boosters close together at the stern rather than splayed.
The wings should sweep back, not out.

blueprints.name: USCSS Nostromo
blueprints.blurb: A brutalist brick of a towing vehicle with a huge engine block and no aerodynamics whatsoever. The best pure hauling platform in the hangar - big slots, big cargo, zero grace.

parts.note: Deep-set industrial bridge, buried in the hull.
+12 inventory slots from the habs alone.
Fore and aft cargo bays.
Towing reactor banks.
The huge rear engine wall.
Attitude and mooring thruster pods strung along the engine wall - also satisfies the two-light-thruster minimum.
Turret clusters.
Boxy stabilisers.
Industrial cladding.

buildTips: Wide, flat and heavy: 3 floors here is actually fine because it is all wall.
The rear engine block should be a solid, unbroken wall of nozzles.
Maximise Habs - this is the blueprint to fly if you want a mobile storage base.
No wings that look aerodynamic. Everything square.

blueprints.name: Thunderbird 2
blueprints.blurb: A big green brick with six landing pads and a belly full of equipment. The easiest large build in the hangar because a Thunderbird is already boxy - and NMS boxy is a feature, not a bug.

parts.note: Nose flight deck with the dropship read.
The cargo body - three floors of module space.
The pod release bay at the belly.
Equipment storage.
Twin pods under the wing roots.
Rescue ships still need one gun.
Four thruster pads plus two nose gears.

buildTips: Three floors, flat box. This is the one blueprint where a 3-floor stack looks correct.
Wing roots sit high and forward, engines hang below them.
Six landing points total - it should look stable enough to hold a small base.
Fill the interior: refiners, storage, a bed. It is a mobile workshop.
